Got it. The inventory came through cleanly. And this is a considerably more interesting sample collection than a generic drum-and-bass folder.

**First inventory pass:**

<grid columns={2} gap={2}>
  <grid-item>
    <box border radius="lg" padding={3}>
      <title size="2xl" tabularNums>147</title>
      <text color="secondary" size="xs">Audio files</text>
    </box>
  </grid-item>
  <grid-item>
    <box border radius="lg" padding={3}>
      <title size="2xl" tabularNums>44</title>
      <text color="secondary" size="xs">Directories represented</text>
    </box>
  </grid-item>
  <grid-item>
    <box border radius="lg" padding={3}>
      <title size="2xl" tabularNums>114 MB</title>
      <text color="secondary" size="xs">Combined file size</text>
    </box>
  </grid-item>
  <grid-item>
    <box border radius="lg" padding={3}>
      <title size="2xl" tabularNums>141 / 6</title>
      <text color="secondary" size="xs">WAV / MP3 files</text>
    </box>
  </grid-item>
</grid>

The filenames reveal several particularly promising sound families:

- **Indian and Central Asian:** sitar, tambura, tabla, Afghan ensemble, bagpipes, Indian percussion and vocal samples.
- **Chinese and East Asian:** traditional music, flutes, spoken voices, chimes.
- **Odd acoustic instruments:** berimbau, jaw harp, gamelan, Tibetan bowls, didgeridoo, autoharp.
- **Electronic and synthetic:** Moog, C64 SID, synth loops, phasing machinery, strange pads.
- **Voices and found material:** chants, spoken samples, singing, granular weirdness.

These are filename-based classifications, not claims that I've listened to the samples yet.

**Important limitation:** the CSV tells me names, locations, extensions and file sizes. It doesn't contain the audio itself, so I can't yet verify timbre, tempo, pitch, duration or musical character.

I'd suggest two passes:

1. **Catalogue pass:** I'll organize all 147 samples into a searchable index, with provisional tags and likely musical uses.
2. **Listening pass:** You can zip `D:\HYPERFLIRT\SAMPLES` and upload it. I'll inspect the actual sounds and refine the catalogue.

The eventual goal is to make a Sonic Pi instrumentarium: a map of what you have, what each sound can do, and how to call it in code. Then Spermolio gets to use the real orchestra.

# SPERMOLIO: metric chamber-folk / underwater crank-rap machine
# Sonic Pi 4.x
#
# This is a deliberately chaotic instrumental realization of the supplied
# direction. There is no voice synthesis here. The lyric text is segmented
# into phrase-sized metric units; a synthetic "mouth" line marks syllabic
# density, accents, rests, slides and sustained endings.
#
# Meter design:
#   Main cycle: 10 eighth-note slots grouped 4 + 3 + 3 (5/4)
#   Alternate slog: 5 quarter-note beats grouped 2 + 2 + 1
#   Tempo: 144 BPM quarter note; 10 eighth slots = 2.083 seconds.
#
# Chord spellings are the user's chord vocabulary:
#   Amin, Cmaj, Eb, Gbmin, C# major, Cm7.
# C# major is voiced enharmonically as Db-F-Ab for MIDI practicality.

use_bpm 144
use_random_seed rrand_i(1, 999999)

# ---------- Chord vocabulary: exact supplied families ----------
define :voicing do |name|
  case name
  when :Amin   then [45, 48, 52, 57]       # A C E A
  when :Cmaj   then [48, 52, 55, 60]       # C E G C
  when :Eb     then [51, 55, 58, 63]       # Eb G Bb Eb
  when :Gbmin  then [42, 45, 49, 54]       # Gb A Db Gb
  when :Csharp then [49, 53, 56, 61]       # C# E# G# C#
  when :Cm7    then [48, 51, 55, 58]       # C Eb G Bb
  else [45, 48, 52, 57]
  end
end

define :root_of do |name|
  voicing(name)[0]
end

# ---------- Metric phrase cells ----------
# Each phrase is represented by 10 eighth-note slots.
# Numbers are relative syllabic events: 0=rest, 1=short, 2=normal,
# 3=stressed/clustered, 4=held syllable. This is a rhythmic proxy,
# not phonetic transcription or actual lyric playback.
#
# Phrase text is preserved as comments to make the mapping editable.
phrases = [
  # "Brings new meaning to the phrase I call shotgun!"
  ["Brings new meaning to the phrase I call shotgun", [3,1,2,1,2,1,3,0,2,4], [:Amin,:Cmaj,:Amin,:Eb,:Eb,:Eb,:Cmaj,:Cmaj,:Eb,:Amin], :Gbmin],

  # "Ok... so back to liquefaction. They discovered benzine..."
  ["Ok so back to liquefaction they discovered benzine because they happened to have the nozzle on the bottom of the compressor", [2,0,1,2,3,1,2,2,1,4], [:Amin,:Cmaj,:Amin,:Eb,:Eb,:Eb,:Cmaj,:Cmaj,:Eb,:Gbmin], :Csharp],

  # "Had it been on the top... they might've noticed a sloshing..."
  ["Had it been on the top they might have noticed a sloshing and judiciously avoided it", [1,2,1,3,0,2,1,3,2,4], [:Amin,:Cmaj,:Amin,:Eb,:Eb,:Eb,:Cmaj,:Cmaj,:Eb,:Eb], :Eb],

  # "Wait. Are benzine and benzene different things?"
  ["Wait are benzine and benzene different things", [3,0,2,1,3,1,2,0,2,4], [:Amin,:Cmaj,:Amin,:Eb,:Eb,:Eb,:Cmaj,:Cmaj,:Eb,:Gbmin], :Eb],

  # Portable oil gas pitch
  ["So portable oil gas basically solves the problem have a nice country manner sick of all that whale oil boiling", [2,1,2,3,1,2,1,3,2,4], [:Amin,:Cmaj,:Amin,:Eb,:Eb,:Eb,:Cmaj,:Cmaj,:Eb,:Gbmin], :Csharp],

  # Victorian timing aside
  ["Wait this was E flat three plus two beat so not Victorian yet I assume", [3,1,2,0,3,1,2,1,2,4], [:Amin,:Cmaj,:Amin,:Eb,:Eb,:Eb,:Cmaj,:Cmaj,:Eb,:Csharp], :Eb],

  # Country lord / whale oil
  ["But presumably before it was commercialized the class conscious country lord actually was trying to boil whale oil at home", [1,2,1,2,3,1,2,1,3,4], [:Amin,:Cmaj,:Amin,:Eb,:Eb,:Eb,:Cmaj,:Cmaj,:Eb,:Gbmin], :Eb],

  # Compressed whale gas question
  ["What was the advantage of compressed whale gas versus liquid whale head extraction", [3,1,2,1,3,1,2,1,2,4], [:Amin,:Cmaj,:Amin,:Eb,:Eb,:Eb,:Cmaj,:Cmaj,:Eb,:Csharp], :Cm7],

  # Spermaceti / spermolio
  ["Spermaceti liquid whale head extraction spermolio tomato tomatalio", [3,1,2,2,3,1,2,1,3,4], [:Amin,:Cmaj,:Amin,:Eb,:Eb,:Eb,:Cmaj,:Cmaj,:Eb,:Csharp], :Amin],

  # Overlooked alternative
  ["I think spermolio is a sadly overlooked alternative", [1,2,1,3,1,2,1,3,2,4], [:Amin,:Cmaj,:Amin,:Eb,:Eb,:Eb,:Cmaj,:Cmaj,:Eb,:Csharp], :Eb],

  # Whale carcass / melon tapping monologue
  ["Sure beats the way we used to do it in my day dragging the whale carcass into the parlor in the morning go out on a fox hunt during the daylight hours to get out of the servant boys way while a crew of sixteen eight to twelve year olds performed the eight hour melon tapping procedure with time for smoke breaks come home light the whale spigot for a nice game of billiards wake up to whale stew in the morning just in time for the days carcass to arrive", [3,1,2,1,3,1,2,3,1,4], [:Amin,:Cmaj,:Amin,:Eb,:Eb,:Eb,:Cmaj,:Cmaj,:Amin,:Gbmin], :Cmaj],

  # Tobacco allowance / Swisher Sweets
  ["Do not forget to budget for the boys smokes and Timmy likes his Swisher Sweets", [1,2,3,1,2,1,3,1,2,4], [:Amin,:Cmaj,:Amin,:Eb,:Eb,:Eb,:Cmaj,:Cmaj,:Amin,:Csharp], :Gbmin],

  # Lol, cheroot, tobacco
  ["Lol cheroot that sounds familiar type of tobacco", [3,0,1,2,2,1,3,0,2,4], [:Amin,:Cmaj,:Amin,:Eb,:Eb,:Eb,:Cmaj,:Cmaj,:Amin,:Csharp], :Cm7],

  # Industrial-age dialogue
  ["And too young to operate the lemonade stand pshaw this is the industrial age good sir no youth is too youth to feed into the gears what do you mistake us for Irish", [1,2,1,3,0,2,3,1,2,4], [:Amin,:Cmaj,:Amin,:Eb,:Eb,:Eb,:Cmaj,:Cmaj,:Amin,:Eb], :Amin],

  # Tobacco allowance / old stogies
  ["Maybe we should cut the boys tobacco allowance let the younger ones fight over old stogies they have found short but not too big around builds character", [2,1,2,3,1,2,1,3,2,4], [:Amin,:Cmaj,:Amin,:Eb,:Eb,:Eb,:Cmaj,:Cmaj,:Amin,:Amin], :Csharp],

  # Timeline aside
  ["I might be jumping ahead a bit in the timeline lyrically speaking", [1,2,1,3,1,2,0,2,2,4], [:Amin,:Cmaj,:Amin,:Eb,:Eb,:Eb,:Cmaj,:Cmaj,:Amin,:Eb], :Amin],

  # Boxcar William
  ["That is Boxcar William to you", [3,1,2,0,3,1,2,0,2,4], [:Amin,:Cmaj,:Amin,:Eb,:Eb,:Eb,:Cmaj,:Cmaj,:Amin,:Gbmin], :Cmaj],

  # Final interruption
  ["Do not make me have my", [1,2,3,1,2,1,3,0,0,4], [:Amin,:Cmaj,:Amin,:Eb,:Eb,:Eb,:Cmaj,:Cmaj,:Amin,:Csharp], :Eb]
]


# ---------- Shared clock ----------
# One cell is 10 eighths = five quarter-note beats.
# All parts advance by the same 5/4 cell, but use different internal accents.

# ---------- Felted-ish piano: actual piano synth, softened ----------
in_thread(name: :piano) do
  use_synth :piano
  with_fx :lpf, cutoff: 88 do
    with_fx :reverb, room: 0.78, mix: 0.30 do
      phrases.each_with_index do |ph, idx|
        # Main chord sequence from the supplied repeated cadence.
        ph[2].each_with_index do |ch, slot|
          ns = voicing(ch)
          # Chord attacks emphasize 4+3+3 group boundaries: 0, 4, 7.
          accent = [0,4,7].include?(slot) ? 0.68 : 0.40
          play_chord ns, attack: 0.015, sustain: (slot == 9 ? 0.9 : 0.34),
            release: 0.42, amp: accent
          sleep 0.5 # eighth-note slot
        end
        # Color chord from the annotation at phrase head, as a brief dissonant flare.
        play_chord voicing(ph[3]), attack: 0.01, sustain: 0.12, release: 0.7, amp: 0.22
      end
    end
  end
end

# ---------- Vibraphone: Pachelbel-ish looping, altered on each return ----------
in_thread(name: :vibraphone) do
  use_synth :pretty_bell
  with_fx :reverb, room: 0.92, mix: 0.42 do
    phrases.each_with_index do |ph, idx|
      base = [74, 77, 79, 77, 74, 72, 70, 72]
      base.each_with_index do |n, i|
        # Refrain-like motif returns with changing emphasis and occasional mutation.
        n = n + choose([-2,0,0,2,5]) if one_in(4)
        amp = ([0,4,7].include?(i) ? 0.38 : 0.19)
        play n, release: (i == 7 ? 1.1 : 0.42), amp: amp
        sleep 0.625
      end
      sleep 0.0
    end
  end
end

# ---------- Singing saw: legato, unstable and slightly seasick ----------
in_thread(name: :singing_saw) do
  use_synth :saw
  with_fx :reverb, room: 0.96, mix: 0.48 do
    with_fx :echo, phase: 0.75, decay: 3.5, mix: 0.22 do
      phrases.each_with_index do |ph, idx|
        root = root_of(ph[2][0])
        saw_notes = [root + 19, root + 22, root + 24, root + 22, root + 19]
        saw_notes.each_with_index do |n, i|
          n = n + choose([-1,0,0,1]) if one_in(3)
          play n, attack: 0.20, sustain: (i == 4 ? 1.0 : 0.55),
            release: 0.9, cutoff: 78, amp: 0.13, slide: 0.18
          sleep 1
        end
      end
    end
  end
end

# ---------- Bagpipe-like underwater drone ----------
in_thread(name: :drone) do
  use_synth :hollow
  with_fx :lpf, cutoff: 58 do
    with_fx :reverb, room: 1, mix: 0.55 do
      phrases.each_with_index do |ph, idx|
        root = root_of(ph[2][0]) - 12
        play root, attack: 0.3, sustain: 3.8, release: 1.0, amp: 0.18
        play root + 7, attack: 0.4, sustain: 3.3, release: 0.9, amp: 0.09
        sleep 5
      end
    end
  end
end

# ---------- Jaw harp / osseophone: plunks, ticks, glitches ----------
in_thread(name: :osseophone) do
  use_synth :pluck
  with_fx :bitcrusher, bits: 5, sample_rate: 11025, mix: 0.28 do
    phrases.each_with_index do |ph, idx|
      10.times do |slot|
        density = ph[1][slot]
        if density >= 2 || one_in(3)
          n = root_of(ph[2][slot]) + choose([0, 7, 12, 19])
          play n, release: rrand(0.06, 0.22), amp: density == 3 ? 0.34 : 0.17
        end
        sleep 0.5
      end
    end
  end
end

# ---------- Percussion: 4+3+3 lilt, then 2+2+1 stomp ----------
in_thread(name: :percussion) do
  phrases.each_with_index do |ph, idx|
    # 10 eighth slots. Group accents at 0, 4, 7 = 4+3+3.
    10.times do |slot|
      if [0,4,7].include?(slot)
        sample :bd_haus, amp: slot == 0 ? 0.52 : 0.27
      elsif [2,6,9].include?(slot)
        sample :elec_tick, amp: 0.14, rate: 0.8
      end
      # Phrase-ending five-beat slog: stronger 2+2+1 accents.
      if idx % 4 == 3 && [0,4,8].include?(slot)
        sample :sn_dolf, amp: [0.26,0.20,0.34][[0,4,8].index(slot)]
      end
      sleep 0.5
    end
  end
end

# ---------- "Vocal" metric proxy: syllabic contour, not speech ----------
# Each lyric phrase becomes ten rhythmic units. Higher density produces
# more attacks; stress values alter accent and pitch; final unit is often held.
in_thread(name: :metric_vocal_proxy) do
  use_synth :tri
  with_fx :reverb, room: 0.55, mix: 0.20 do
    phrases.each_with_index do |ph, idx|
      base = root_of(ph[2][0]) + 24
      ph[1].each_with_index do |weight, slot|
        if weight > 0
          # Three neighboring pitches create a mumble-rap / declamatory contour.
          offset = case weight
                   when 1 then choose([0,2])
                   when 2 then choose([0,2,3,5])
                   when 3 then choose([0,5,7,10])
                   else choose([0,2,5,7])
                   end
          dur = weight == 4 ? 0.42 : (weight == 3 ? 0.20 : 0.12)
          play base + offset, attack: 0.015, sustain: dur,
            release: weight == 4 ? 0.48 : 0.12,
            amp: weight == 3 ? 0.32 : (weight == 4 ? 0.25 : 0.16),
            slide: weight == 4 ? 0.12 : 0.03
        end
        sleep 0.5
      end
    end
  end
end

# ---------- Performance note ----------
# The first item in each phrase array is the lyric metric unit. They are not
# spoken or sung by Sonic Pi. To add real voice later, record or import a
# vocal track and align its phrase attacks to the same 10-slot cells.

# Sonic Pi 4.x
#
# This is a deliberately chaotic instrumental realization of the supplied
# direction. There is no voice synthesis here. The lyric text is segmented
# into phrase-sized metric units; a synthetic "mouth" line marks syllabic
# density, accents, rests, slides and sustained endings.
#
# Meter design:
#   Main cycle: 10 eighth-note slots grouped 4 + 3 + 3 (5/4)
#   Alternate slog: 5 quarter-note beats grouped 2 + 2 + 1
#   Tempo: 144 BPM quarter note; 10 eighth slots = 2.083 seconds.
#
# Chord spellings are the user's chord vocabulary:
#   Amin, Cmaj, Eb, Gbmin, C# major, Cm7.
# C# major is voiced enharmonically as Db-F-Ab for MIDI practicality.

use_bpm 144
use_random_seed rrand_i(1, 999999)

# ---------- Chord vocabulary: exact supplied families ----------
define :voicing do |name|
  case name
  when :Amin   then [45, 48, 52, 57]       # A C E A
  when :Cmaj   then [48, 52, 55, 60]       # C E G C
  when :Eb     then [51, 55, 58, 63]       # Eb G Bb Eb
  when :Gbmin  then [42, 45, 49, 54]       # Gb A Db Gb
  when :Csharp then [49, 53, 56, 61]       # C# E# G# C#
  when :Cm7    then [48, 51, 55, 58]       # C Eb G Bb
  else [45, 48, 52, 57]
  end
end

define :root_of do |name|
  voicing(name)[0]
end

# ---------- Metric phrase cells ----------
# Each phrase is represented by 10 eighth-note slots.
# Numbers are relative syllabic events: 0=rest, 1=short, 2=normal,
# 3=stressed/clustered, 4=held syllable. This is a rhythmic proxy,
# not phonetic transcription or actual lyric playback.
#
# Phrase text is preserved as comments to make the mapping editable.
phrases = [
  # "Brings new meaning to the phrase I call shotgun!"
  ["Brings new meaning to the phrase I call shotgun", [3,1,2,1,2,1,3,0,2,4], [:Amin,:Cmaj,:Amin,:Eb,:Eb,:Eb,:Cmaj,:Cmaj,:Eb,:Amin], :Gbmin],

  # "Ok... so back to liquefaction. They discovered benzine..."
  ["Ok so back to liquefaction they discovered benzine because they happened to have the nozzle on the bottom of the compressor", [2,0,1,2,3,1,2,2,1,4], [:Amin,:Cmaj,:Amin,:Eb,:Eb,:Eb,:Cmaj,:Cmaj,:Eb,:Gbmin], :Csharp],

  # "Had it been on the top... they might've noticed a sloshing..."
  ["Had it been on the top they might have noticed a sloshing and judiciously avoided it", [1,2,1,3,0,2,1,3,2,4], [:Amin,:Cmaj,:Amin,:Eb,:Eb,:Eb,:Cmaj,:Cmaj,:Eb,:Eb], :Eb],

  # "Wait. Are benzine and benzene different things?"
  ["Wait are benzine and benzene different things", [3,0,2,1,3,1,2,0,2,4], [:Amin,:Cmaj,:Amin,:Eb,:Eb,:Eb,:Cmaj,:Cmaj,:Eb,:Gbmin], :Eb],

  # Portable oil gas pitch
  ["So portable oil gas basically solves the problem have a nice country manner sick of all that whale oil boiling", [2,1,2,3,1,2,1,3,2,4], [:Amin,:Cmaj,:Amin,:Eb,:Eb,:Eb,:Cmaj,:Cmaj,:Eb,:Gbmin], :Csharp],

  # Victorian timing aside
  ["Wait this was E flat three plus two beat so not Victorian yet I assume", [3,1,2,0,3,1,2,1,2,4], [:Amin,:Cmaj,:Amin,:Eb,:Eb,:Eb,:Cmaj,:Cmaj,:Eb,:Csharp], :Eb],

  # Country lord / whale oil
  ["But presumably before it was commercialized the class conscious country lord actually was trying to boil whale oil at home", [1,2,1,2,3,1,2,1,3,4], [:Amin,:Cmaj,:Amin,:Eb,:Eb,:Eb,:Cmaj,:Cmaj,:Eb,:Gbmin], :Eb],

  # Compressed whale gas question
  ["What was the advantage of compressed whale gas versus liquid whale head extraction", [3,1,2,1,3,1,2,1,2,4], [:Amin,:Cmaj,:Amin,:Eb,:Eb,:Eb,:Cmaj,:Cmaj,:Eb,:Csharp], :Cm7],

  # Spermaceti / spermolio
  ["Spermaceti liquid whale head extraction spermolio tomato tomatalio", [3,1,2,2,3,1,2,1,3,4], [:Amin,:Cmaj,:Amin,:Eb,:Eb,:Eb,:Cmaj,:Cmaj,:Eb,:Csharp], :Amin],

  # Overlooked alternative
  ["I think spermolio is a sadly overlooked alternative", [1,2,1,3,1,2,1,3,2,4], [:Amin,:Cmaj,:Amin,:Eb,:Eb,:Eb,:Cmaj,:Cmaj,:Eb,:Csharp], :Eb],

  # Whale carcass / melon tapping monologue
  ["Sure beats the way we used to do it in my day dragging the whale carcass into the parlor in the morning go out on a fox hunt during the daylight hours to get out of the servant boys way while a crew of sixteen eight to twelve year olds performed the eight hour melon tapping procedure with time for smoke breaks come home light the whale spigot for a nice game of billiards wake up to whale stew in the morning just in time for the days carcass to arrive", [3,1,2,1,3,1,2,3,1,4], [:Amin,:Cmaj,:Amin,:Eb,:Eb,:Eb,:Cmaj,:Cmaj,:Amin,:Gbmin], :Cmaj],

  # Tobacco allowance / Swisher Sweets
  ["Do not forget to budget for the boys smokes and Timmy likes his Swisher Sweets", [1,2,3,1,2,1,3,1,2,4], [:Amin,:Cmaj,:Amin,:Eb,:Eb,:Eb,:Cmaj,:Cmaj,:Amin,:Csharp], :Gbmin],

  # Lol, cheroot, tobacco
  ["Lol cheroot that sounds familiar type of tobacco", [3,0,1,2,2,1,3,0,2,4], [:Amin,:Cmaj,:Amin,:Eb,:Eb,:Eb,:Cmaj,:Cmaj,:Amin,:Csharp], :Cm7],

  # Industrial-age dialogue
  ["And too young to operate the lemonade stand pshaw this is the industrial age good sir no youth is too youth to feed into the gears what do you mistake us for Irish", [1,2,1,3,0,2,3,1,2,4], [:Amin,:Cmaj,:Amin,:Eb,:Eb,:Eb,:Cmaj,:Cmaj,:Amin,:Eb], :Amin],

  # Tobacco allowance / old stogies
  ["Maybe we should cut the boys tobacco allowance let the younger ones fight over old stogies they have found short but not too big around builds character", [2,1,2,3,1,2,1,3,2,4], [:Amin,:Cmaj,:Amin,:Eb,:Eb,:Eb,:Cmaj,:Cmaj,:Amin,:Amin], :Csharp],

  # Timeline aside
  ["I might be jumping ahead a bit in the timeline lyrically speaking", [1,2,1,3,1,2,0,2,2,4], [:Amin,:Cmaj,:Amin,:Eb,:Eb,:Eb,:Cmaj,:Cmaj,:Amin,:Eb], :Amin],

  # Boxcar William
  ["That is Boxcar William to you", [3,1,2,0,3,1,2,0,2,4], [:Amin,:Cmaj,:Amin,:Eb,:Eb,:Eb,:Cmaj,:Cmaj,:Amin,:Gbmin], :Cmaj],

  # Final interruption
  ["Do not make me have my", [1,2,3,1,2,1,3,0,0,4], [:Amin,:Cmaj,:Amin,:Eb,:Eb,:Eb,:Cmaj,:Cmaj,:Amin,:Csharp], :Eb]
]


# ---------- Shared clock ----------
# One cell is 10 eighths = five quarter-note beats.
# All parts advance by the same 5/4 cell, but use different internal accents.

# ---------- Felted-ish piano: actual piano synth, softened ----------
in_thread(name: :piano) do
  use_synth :piano
  with_fx :lpf, cutoff: 88 do
    with_fx :reverb, room: 0.78, mix: 0.30 do
      phrases.each_with_index do |ph, idx|
        # Main chord sequence from the supplied repeated cadence.
        ph[2].each_with_index do |ch, slot|
          ns = voicing(ch)
          # Chord attacks emphasize 4+3+3 group boundaries: 0, 4, 7.
          accent = [0,4,7].include?(slot) ? 0.68 : 0.40
          play_chord ns, attack: 0.015, sustain: (slot == 9 ? 0.9 : 0.34),
            release: 0.42, amp: accent
          sleep 0.5 # eighth-note slot
        end
        # Color chord from the annotation at phrase head, as a brief dissonant flare.
        play_chord voicing(ph[3]), attack: 0.01, sustain: 0.12, release: 0.7, amp: 0.22
      end
    end
  end
end

# ---------- Vibraphone: Pachelbel-ish looping, altered on each return ----------
in_thread(name: :vibraphone) do
  use_synth :pretty_bell
  with_fx :reverb, room: 0.92, mix: 0.42 do
    phrases.each_with_index do |ph, idx|
      base = [74, 77, 79, 77, 74, 72, 70, 72]
      base.each_with_index do |n, i|
        # Refrain-like motif returns with changing emphasis and occasional mutation.
        n = n + choose([-2,0,0,2,5]) if one_in(4)
        amp = ([0,4,7].include?(i) ? 0.38 : 0.19)
        play n, release: (i == 7 ? 1.1 : 0.42), amp: amp
        sleep 0.625
      end
      sleep 0.0
    end
  end
end

# ---------- Singing saw: legato, unstable and slightly seasick ----------
in_thread(name: :singing_saw) do
  use_synth :saw
  with_fx :reverb, room: 0.96, mix: 0.48 do
    with_fx :echo, phase: 0.75, decay: 3.5, mix: 0.22 do
      phrases.each_with_index do |ph, idx|
        root = root_of(ph[2][0])
        saw_notes = [root + 19, root + 22, root + 24, root + 22, root + 19]
        saw_notes.each_with_index do |n, i|
          n = n + choose([-1,0,0,1]) if one_in(3)
          play n, attack: 0.20, sustain: (i == 4 ? 1.0 : 0.55),
            release: 0.9, cutoff: 78, amp: 0.13, slide: 0.18
          sleep 1
        end
      end
    end
  end
end

# ---------- Bagpipe-like underwater drone ----------
in_thread(name: :drone) do
  use_synth :hollow
  with_fx :lpf, cutoff: 58 do
    with_fx :reverb, room: 1, mix: 0.55 do
      phrases.each_with_index do |ph, idx|
        root = root_of(ph[2][0]) - 12
        play root, attack: 0.3, sustain: 3.8, release: 1.0, amp: 0.18
        play root + 7, attack: 0.4, sustain: 3.3, release: 0.9, amp: 0.09
        sleep 5
      end
    end
  end
end

# ---------- Jaw harp / osseophone: plunks, ticks, glitches ----------
in_thread(name: :osseophone) do
  use_synth :pluck
  with_fx :bitcrusher, bits: 5, sample_rate: 11025, mix: 0.28 do
    phrases.each_with_index do |ph, idx|
      10.times do |slot|
        density = ph[1][slot]
        if density >= 2 || one_in(3)
          n = root_of(ph[2][slot]) + choose([0, 7, 12, 19])
          play n, release: rrand(0.06, 0.22), amp: density == 3 ? 0.34 : 0.17
        end
        sleep 0.5
      end
    end
  end
end

# ---------- Percussion: 4+3+3 lilt, then 2+2+1 stomp ----------
in_thread(name: :percussion) do
  phrases.each_with_index do |ph, idx|
    # 10 eighth slots. Group accents at 0, 4, 7 = 4+3+3.
    10.times do |slot|
      if [0,4,7].include?(slot)
        sample :bd_haus, amp: slot == 0 ? 0.52 : 0.27
      elsif [2,6,9].include?(slot)
        sample :elec_tick, amp: 0.14, rate: 0.8
      end
      # Phrase-ending five-beat slog: stronger 2+2+1 accents.
      if idx % 4 == 3 && [0,4,8].include?(slot)
        sample :sn_dolf, amp: [0.26,0.20,0.34][[0,4,8].index(slot)]
      end
      sleep 0.5
    end
  end
end

# ---------- "Vocal" metric proxy: syllabic contour, not speech ----------
# Each lyric phrase becomes ten rhythmic units. Higher density produces
# more attacks; stress values alter accent and pitch; final unit is often held.
in_thread(name: :metric_vocal_proxy) do
  use_synth :tri
  with_fx :reverb, room: 0.55, mix: 0.20 do
    phrases.each_with_index do |ph, idx|
      base = root_of(ph[2][0]) + 24
      ph[1].each_with_index do |weight, slot|
        if weight > 0
          # Three neighboring pitches create a mumble-rap / declamatory contour.
          offset = case weight
                   when 1 then choose([0,2])
                   when 2 then choose([0,2,3,5])
                   when 3 then choose([0,5,7,10])
                   else choose([0,2,5,7])
                   end
          dur = weight == 4 ? 0.42 : (weight == 3 ? 0.20 : 0.12)
          play base + offset, attack: 0.015, sustain: dur,
            release: weight == 4 ? 0.48 : 0.12,
            amp: weight == 3 ? 0.32 : (weight == 4 ? 0.25 : 0.16),
            slide: weight == 4 ? 0.12 : 0.03
        end
        sleep 0.5
      end
    end
  end
end

# ---------- Performance note ----------
# The first item in each phrase array is the lyric metric unit. They are not
# spoken or sung by Sonic Pi. To add real voice later, record or import a
# vocal track and align its phrase attacks to the same 10-slot cells.

bash -lc cat > /mnt/data/Spermolio_Sample_Orchestra.rb <<'RUBY'
# SPERMOLIO: Sample Orchestra Edition
# Sonic Pi 4.x
#
# Uses filenames from D:\HYPERFLIRT\SAMPLES as a guide. The sample choices
# are hypotheses based on names, not auditioned or verified descriptions.
# All paths below are absolute Windows paths written with forward slashes.
#
# Main metric cell: 10 eighth-note slots grouped 4+3+3 (five quarter beats).
# Every fourth cell gets a more forceful 2+2+1 stomp overlay.
# Tempo: 144 BPM.

use_bpm 144
use_random_seed rrand_i(1, 999999)

# ---------- Chord vocabulary from the earlier prompt ----------
define :voicing do |name|
  case name
  when :Amin   then [45, 48, 52, 57]
  when :Cmaj   then [48, 52, 55, 60]
  when :Eb     then [51, 55, 58, 63]
  when :Gbmin  then [42, 45, 49, 54]
  when :Csharp then [49, 53, 56, 61]
  when :Cm7    then [48, 51, 55, 58]
  else [45, 48, 52, 57]
  end
end

define :root_of do |name|
  voicing(name)[0]
end

# ---------- Lyric-derived metric cells ----------
# [phrase label, 10-slot stress/density contour, 10 chord hits, color chord]
# This is a rhythmic proxy, not a phonetic transcription or actual singing.
phrases = [

# ---------- Sample palette: loops ----------

in_thread(name: :sitar_world_loop) do

in_thread(name: :saz_and_sitar) do

      end
      if one_in(2)
        sample "D:/HYPERFLIRT/SAMPLES/INSTRUMENTS (SINGLE SAMPLES)/big_dissonant_round_bell.wav",
          rate: choose([0.75, 1.0, 1.25]), amp: 0.12
      end
      sleep 5
    end
  end
end

# ---------- Piano chord spine and synth shadow ----------
in_thread(name: :piano_spine) do
  use_synth :piano
  with_fx :lpf, cutoff: 88 do
    with_fx :reverb, room: 0.78, mix: 0.30 do
      phrases.each do |ph|
        ph[2].each_with_index do |ch, slot|
          accent = [0,4,7].include?(slot) ? 0.52 : 0.27
          play_chord voicing(ch), attack: 0.015,
            sustain: (slot == 9 ? 0.7 : 0.25), release: 0.35, amp: accent
          sleep 0.5
        end
        play_chord voicing(ph[3]), attack: 0.01, sustain: 0.1, release: 0.65, amp: 0.16
      end
    end
  end
end

in_thread(name: :saw_shadow) do
  use_synth :saw
  with_fx :echo, phase: 0.75, decay: 3.2, mix: 0.2 do
    phrases.each do |ph|
      root = root_of(ph[2][0])
      saw_notes = [root + 19, root + 22, root + 24, root + 22, root + 19]
      saw_notes.each_with_index do |pitch, pos|
        play pitch + choose([-1,0,0,1]), attack: 0.18,
          sustain: (pos == 4 ? 0.8 : 0.42), release: 0.7,
          cutoff: 78, amp: 0.10
        sleep 1
      end
    end
  end
end

# ---------- Percussion: real sample hits over the loop beds ----------
in_thread(name: :sampled_percussion) do
  phrases.each_with_index do |ph, idx|
    10.times do |slot|
      if [0,4,7].include?(slot)
        sample "D:/HYPERFLIRT/SAMPLES/DRUMS (SINGLE HITS)/Snares/tinyelectrosd.wav",
          rate: slot == 0 ? 0.82 : 0.65, amp: slot == 0 ? 0.23 : 0.13
      elsif [2,6,9].include?(slot)
        sample "D:/HYPERFLIRT/SAMPLES/DRUMS (SINGLE HITS)/African and Eastern Percussion/pipechimes.wav",
          rate: choose([0.8, 1.0, 1.25]), amp: 0.12
      end
      if idx % 4 == 3 && [0,4,8].include?(slot)
        sample "D:/HYPERFLIRT/SAMPLES/DRUMS (FULL KITS)/ETHNIC and WORLD PERCUSSION/Clay Pots/Small-pot-hand.wav",
          rate: [0.85, 0.7, 1.15][[0,4,8].index(slot)], amp: 0.25
      end
      if one_in(9)
        sample "D:/HYPERFLIRT/SAMPLES/DRUMS (SINGLE HITS)/Weird and Interesting Hits/crazysquirt.wav",
          rate: rrand(0.65, 1.4), amp: 0.10
      end
      sleep 0.5
    end
  end
end

# ---------- Metric vocal proxy: retains the earlier lyric-shaped rhythm ----------
in_thread(name: :metric_vocal_proxy) do
  use_synth :tri
  with_fx :reverb, room: 0.55, mix: 0.20 do
    phrases.each do |ph|
      base = root_of(ph[2][0]) + 24
      ph[1].each do |weight|
        if weight > 0
          offset = case weight
                   when 1 then choose([0,2])
                   when 2 then choose([0,2,3,5])
                   when 3 then choose([0,5,7,10])
                   else choose([0,2,5,7])
                   end
          dur = weight == 4 ? 0.42 : (weight == 3 ? 0.20 : 0.12)
          play base + offset, attack: 0.015, sustain: dur,
            release: weight == 4 ? 0.48 : 0.12,
            amp: weight == 3 ? 0.25 : (weight == 4 ? 0.20 : 0.12)
        end
        sleep 0.5
      end
    end
  end
end

# ---------- Occasional freak events ----------
in_thread(name: :mechanical_intrusions) do
  phrases.each_with_index do |ph, idx|
    if idx % 6 == 2
      sample "D:/HYPERFLIRT/SAMPLES/SOUND EFFECTS and NOISES/Electro and Synthetic/crazy-machine-junk.mp3",
        rate: choose([0.8, 1.0, 1.2]), amp: 0.12, pan: -0.2
    end
    if idx % 7 == 4
      sample "D:/HYPERFLIRT/SAMPLES/LOOPING AMBIENCE/crazy-making-loopy-creature.wav",
        beat_stretch: 5, amp: 0.10, pan: 0.25
    end
    if idx % 5 == 3
      sample "D:/HYPERFLIRT/SAMPLES/INSTRUMENTS (SINGLE SAMPLES)/mini-moog-low-c.wav",
        rate: choose([0.5, 0.75, 1.0]), amp: 0.16
    end
    sleep 5
  end
end

ps_script = r'''# Hyperflirt recursive audio inventory
# Scans D:\HYPERFLIRT and writes reports to your Documents folder.
# It does not modify, move, rename, or open the audio files.

$Root = "D:\HYPERFLIRT"
$OutputFolder = [Environment]::GetFolderPath("MyDocuments")

if (-not (Test-Path -LiteralPath $Root -PathType Container)) {
    throw "Cannot find the source folder: $Root"
}
if (-not (Test-Path -LiteralPath $OutputFolder -PathType Container)) {
    New-Item -ItemType Directory -Path $OutputFolder -Force | Out-Null
}

$AudioExtensions = @(
    ".wav", ".wave", ".aif", ".aiff", ".flac", ".ogg", ".opus",
    ".mp3", ".m4a", ".aac", ".wma", ".a​​pe", ".alac"
)
$ArchiveExtensions = @(".zip", ".7z", ".rar", ".tar", ".gz")

Write-Host "Scanning $Root ..."
$allFiles = Get-ChildItem -LiteralPath $Root -Recurse -File -Force -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue

$audio = $allFiles | Where-Object {
    $AudioExtensions -contains $_.Extension.ToLowerInvariant()
} | ForEach-Object {
    $relative = $_.FullName.Substring($Root.TrimEnd('\').Length).TrimStart('\')
    [PSCustomObject]@{
        RelativePath = $relative
        Folder       = $_.DirectoryName
        Filename     = $_.Name
        Extension    = $_.Extension.ToLowerInvariant()
        SizeBytes    = $_.Length
        SizeMB       = [math]::Round($_.Length / 1MB, 3)
        Modified     = $_.LastWriteTime
    }
} | Sort-Object RelativePath

$archives = $allFiles | Where-Object {
    $ArchiveExtensions -contains $_.Extension.ToLowerInvariant()
} | ForEach-Object {
    $relative = $_.FullName.Substring($Root.TrimEnd('\').Length).TrimStart('\')
    [PSCustomObject]@{
        RelativePath = $relative
        Filename     = $_.Name
        Extension    = $_.Extension.ToLowerInvariant()
        SizeBytes    = $_.Length
        SizeMB       = [math]::Round($_.Length / 1MB, 3)
        Modified     = $_.LastWriteTime
    }
} | Sort-Object RelativePath

$folderSummary = $audio | Group-Object Folder | ForEach-Object {
    $totalBytes = ($_.Group | Measure-Object -Property SizeBytes -Sum).Sum
    [PSCustomObject]@{
        Folder       = $_.Name
        AudioFiles   = $_.Count
        TotalSizeMB  = [math]::Round($totalBytes / 1MB, 2)
        Extensions   = (($_.Group | Group-Object Extension | Sort-Object Name | ForEach-Object {
            "$($_.Name):$($_.Count)"
        }) -join "; ")
    }
} | Sort-Object Folder

$audioPath = Join-Path $OutputFolder "Hyperflirt_Audio_Inventory.csv"
$folderPath = Join-Path $OutputFolder "Hyperflirt_Folder_Summary.csv"
$archivePath = Join-Path $OutputFolder "Hyperflirt_Archive_Inventory.csv"

$audio | Export-Csv -LiteralPath $audioPath -NoTypeInformation -Encoding UTF8
$folderSummary | Export-Csv -LiteralPath $folderPath -NoTypeInformation -Encoding UTF8
$archives | Export-Csv -LiteralPath $archivePath -NoTypeInformation -Encoding UTF8

$totalMB = [math]::Round((($audio | Measure-Object -Property SizeBytes -Sum).Sum) / 1MB, 2)

Write-Host ""
Write-Host "COMPLETE"
Write-Host "Audio files: $($audio.Count)"
Write-Host "Audio size:  $totalMB MB"
Write-Host "Folders:     $($folderSummary.Count)"
Write-Host "Archives:    $($archives.Count)"
Write-Host ""
Write-Host "Reports saved to:"
Write-Host $audioPath
Write-Host $folderPath
Write-Host $archivePath
'''
# Remove accidental zero-width character from ape extension
ps_script=ps_script.replace(".a​​pe", ".ape")
script_path='/mnt/data/Hyperflirt_Audio_Map.ps1'
with open(script_path,'w',encoding='utf-8-sig') as f: f.write(ps_script)
print(len(ps_script), script_path)

Excellent. I've got the actual sample files now, not just their names. That gives us a way to move beyond filename-based guesses and audition individual sounds when we need to.

## 1. The supplied sample archive

I inspected `samples.zip`, including its nested ZIP archives.

The archive has some interesting structural groupings:

| Category | Audio files |
|---|---:|

| Melodic loops | 13 |
| Drum loops and breaks | 10 |
| Melodic samples | 10 |
| Full drum kits | 9 |
| Organs | 9 |

The root-level files are particularly worth investigating because they don't necessarily fit the archive's more orderly taxonomy.

## 2. The entire Hyperflirt directory

Here's the scanner. It will recursively map loose audio files throughout `D:\HYPERFLIRT`, including your Suno songs and other audio material.

<box border radius="lg" padding={3} gap={2}>
  **Hyperflirt Audio Mapper**
  <text color="secondary" size="xs">PowerShell script · Windows · Read-only scan</text>
  [Download Hyperflirt_Audio_Map.ps1](sandbox:/mnt/data/Hyperflirt_Audio_Map.ps1)
</box>

### Running it

1. Download the `.ps1` file.
2. Open PowerShell.
3. Run:

```powershell
powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File "$env:USERPROFILE\Downloads\Hyperflirt_Audio_Map.ps1"
```

It scans the entire directory and creates three reports in your Documents folder:

| Report | Contents |
|---|---|
| `Hyperflirt_Audio_Inventory.csv` | Every discovered audio file, its path, extension, size and modification date |
| `Hyperflirt_Folder_Summary.csv` | File counts and total size by folder |
| `Hyperflirt_Archive_Inventory.csv` | ZIP, 7z, RAR and other archive files |

It doesn't move, rename, modify or play anything.

**One important distinction:** the scanner catalogs loose audio files, and lists compressed archives separately. It does not unpack every archive on your drive. We can selectively investigate those afterward.

## 3. What I want to do with the resulting map

I suggest we build a proper Hyperflirt audio atlas, with several distinct layers:

- **Suno productions:** your generated songs, grouped by folder and possibly by filename conventions, date and version.
- **Sample library:** instruments, loops, percussion, vocals and effects.
- **Other audio:** recordings, reference material, found sounds and miscellaneous material.
- **Archive contents:** compressed collections that haven't been unpacked.
- **Relationships:** samples that appear in multiple collections, alternate versions, related projects and possible source material.

Eventually, I want to be able to answer questions like: *Find me a vocal phrase that would work against that gamelan loop*, or *Which of my existing Suno tracks uses a similar rhythmic structure?*

That turns Hyperflirt from a very large pile of audio into a searchable creative resource.

Upload the three CSV reports when the scan finishes. We can start building the atlas from there.

# derive top-level area and conservative classification
import re, os
def top_area(folder):
    rel = re.sub(r'^[A-Za-z]:\\HYPERFLIRT\\?', '', str(folder), flags=re.I)
    if rel == str(folder) or rel == "": return "ROOT"
    return rel.split("\\")[0]

def classify(row):
    folder=str(row["Folder"]).lower()
    name=str(row["Filename"]).lower()
    path=folder+"\\"+name
    if any(x in path for x in ["suno", "new album", "singles", "hyperflirt [final]", "middlin", "three", "my tracks", "aiva"]):
        return "Music projects / generated tracks"
    if "sample" in path or "instrument" in path or "loop" in path or "drum" in path:
        return "Samples / sound library"
    if any(x in path for x in ["sonic pi", "experiments"]):
        return "Sonic Pi / experiments"
    if any(x in path for x in ["manuscript", "audio fiction", "tvnk"]):
        return "Narrative / research / TVNK"
    if any(x in path for x in ["misc_recordings", "audio"]):
        return "Recordings / miscellaneous audio"
    return "Unclassified / inspect"
a2=a.copy()
a2["TopLevelArea"]=a2["Folder"].apply(top_area)
a2["ProvisionalCategory"]=a2.apply(classify,axis=1)
a2["RelativePath"]=a2["RelativePath"].astype(str)
a2.to_csv("/mnt/data/Hyperflirt_Audio_Atlas.csv",index=False)
summary=a2.groupby(["TopLevelArea","ProvisionalCategory"]).agg(AudioFiles=("Filename","count"),TotalSizeMB=("SizeMB","sum"),Extensions=("Extension",lambda s:"; ".join(f"{k}:{v}" for k,v in s.value_counts().items()))).reset_index()
summary.to_csv("/mnt/data/Hyperflirt_Audio_Atlas_Summary.csv",index=False)
summary.sort_values("AudioFiles",ascending=False), a2.ProvisionalCategory.value_counts(), a2.TopLevelArea.value_counts().head(20)

parts: We don't need to do any of that. We just use them as raw material and see what happens

Exactly. I was starting to turn a playground into an archival institution. We don't need that.

**Hyperflirt is a resource pool, not a preservation project.**

The working principle:

- Find something interesting by name, folder, or whatever happens to catch our attention.
- Throw it into an arrangement.
- Combine it with things that seem incompatible.
- Distort, stretch, chop, layer, reverse, pitch-shift, or otherwise abuse it.
- Keep the accidents that work. Discard the rest.

No need to classify every sound before using it. No need to identify every track before sampling it. No need to impose a genre or destination.

I'll treat the audio atlas as a map of available raw material, not a mandate to catalogue it. When we write Sonic Pi, we'll draw directly from the collection and let the combinations dictate what happens.

**Next Spermolio can be built from the entire Hyperflirt ecosystem.** Not just the samples folder. The Suno songs are fair game too.

parts: Ok... and... let's give it a new name lol

Oh, absolutely. Spermolio has served its purpose. Time for a rebranding.

Given the musical creature we've assembled, I'd lean toward something that sounds like it might be an obscure musical tradition, a dubious Victorian invention, or a disorder documented in a very unreliable medical journal.

Here are some candidates:

| Name | Character |
|---|---|
| **The Gloaming Engine** | Mechanical, folkloric, vaguely ominous |
| **Bunglepunk** | Unruly, percussive, cheerfully deranged |
| **Osseophonica** | Bone-resonant experimental chamber music |
| **The Unreasonable Orchestra** | A grand collection of bad decisions |
| **Chamber of Horrors** | Victorian musical grotesquerie |
| **Flummoxophone** | Instrumental nonsense with serious ambitions |
| **The Crooked Quadrille** | Lopsided dance music from another century |
| **Mammoth Chutney** | Unclassifiable, faintly gastronomic |
| **The Hypnagogic Foundry** | Dream logic meets industrial machinery |
| **Grumbleton's Patent Music** | An invention nobody should have licensed |

My personal shortlist:

1. **Osseophonica**
2. **The Crooked Quadrille**
3. **Grumbleton's Patent Music**

But I have a suspicion that the right name hasn't been invented yet. What direction appeals: mock-historical, pseudo-scientific, musical nonsense, or something entirely different?
